subtitle: Songs at the doorstep of God

panels.shot: low-angle wide of temple gate at dusk, figures small before towering shikhara
panels.action: Chokhamela & Soyarabai stand at the stone threshold of Pandharpur, hands folded, barred by a shadowy doorway as the temple rises bright beyond.

dialogue.text: In fourteenth-century Maharashtra, Chokhamela and Soyarabai sing to Vitthal from outside the temple door—until their words themselves become a monument on the threshold.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी के महाराष्ट्र में, चोखामेला और सोयाराबाई मंदिर के बाहर से विठ्ठल को गाते हैं — जब तक उनके शब्द ही देहलीज़ पर स्मारक नहीं बन जाते।

panels.shot: wide rural landscape, early morning, showing Mahar hamlet near fertile fields
panels.action: Mist lies over fields near Mehuna Raja as a small Mahar hamlet of earthen houses crouches beside larger village homes and the distant fort-town.

dialogue.text: Around 1300, in villages like Mehuna Raja, Mahar families live on the margins—bound to watch the fields, to serve the settlement, marked as untouchable by caste.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1300 में, मेहूना राजा जैसे गाँवों में महार परिवार खेतों के पहरेदार, बस्ती के नौकर, और जाति से अछूत ठहराए गए हाशिये पर जीते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of young Chokhamela in field, Soyarabai in background near hut
panels.action: A younger Chokhamela leans on a staff at the edge of a field, rough clothes dusty, eyes lifted to the sky, while Soyarabai moves between a hut and a water pot behind him.

dialogue.text: Hagiographers later weave miracles around his birth, but the songs remember something simpler: a Mahar farmhand whose work and humiliation shape every line of his prayer.

i18n.hi: बाद के भक्त-चरित्र उसके जन्म के चारों तरफ चमत्कार बुनते हैं, पर उसके गीत याद रखते हैं एक सीधी बात: खेतों में काम करने वाला महार मज़दूर, जिसकी मेहनत और बेइज़्ज़ती हर प्रार्थना में दर्ज है।

panels.shot: close-up on Chokhamela’s face, contemplative, with faint temple silhouette in distance
panels.action: Chokhamela pauses on a dusty path, a distant temple spire faint on the horizon; his face is lined with worry and wonder, palms pressed together.

dialogue.text: In his abhangas, Chokhamela names his caste openly: “I am a Mahar, I carry sin on my head.” The confession is not surrender—it is an accusation hurled at the social order.

i18n.hi: अपनी अभंगों में चोखामेला अपनी जाति का नाम खुद लेते हैं: "मैं महार हूँ, पाप मेरे सिर पर है।" ये स्वीकारोक्ति हार नहीं है — समाज के ढाँचे पर फेंका गया आरोप है।

panels.shot: intimate interior of humble hut, Soyarabai seated grinding grain, Chokhamela reciting softly
panels.action: Inside their dim hut, Soyarabai grinds grain, listening as Chokhamela sits cross-legged, eyes closed, whispering verses into the warmth of the small room.

dialogue.speaker: Soyarabai
dialogue.text: Vitthal hears you, Chokha. Even if others do not.

i18n.hi: विठ्ठल तुम्हें सुनता है, चोखा। चाहे और कोई न सुने।

panels.shot: pilgrim’s road wide shot, with Warkari crowd walking, couple joining at edge
panels.action: A long line of Warkari pilgrims stretches along the dusty road to Pandharpur, cymbals and veenas in hand; Chokhamela and Soyarabai step into the line at its edge, tentative but hopeful.

dialogue.text: By Chokhamela’s time, Warkari devotion to Vitthal is spreading on foot. Farmers, workers, women walk together, singing abhangas that promise a God close to the poor.

i18n.hi: चोखामेला के समय तक विठ्ठल की वारी पैदल फैल रही है। किसान, मज़दूर, औरतें साथ चलते हैं, अभंग गाते हैं जो एक ऐसे भगवान का वादा करते हैं जो गरीबों के पास रहता है।

panels.shot: busy outer courtyard of Pandharpur temple, couple held back near entrance
panels.action: At Pandharpur’s crowded outer courtyard, Brahmin priests and guards direct upper-caste pilgrims inside while Chokhamela and Soyarabai stand to one side, halted by a stern arm and averted eyes.

dialogue.text: Yet the road ends at a wall. In the fourteenth century, caste rules keep Mahars from the sanctum. The threshold becomes their place—not by choice, but by a guard’s gesture.

i18n.hi: पर रास्ता एक दीवार पर आकर रुकता है। चौदहवीं सदी में जाति के नियम महारों को गर्भगृह से दूर रखते हैं। देहलीज़ ही उनकी जगह बनती है — चाह से नहीं, पहरेदार की रोक से।

panels.shot: low-angle close showing their feet at stone step, inner hall glowing beyond
panels.action: Their bare feet rest on the cold stone step of the doorway; beyond, the hall glows with lamps and garlands around Vitthal’s unseen image.

dialogue.text: Standing at the very edge of the doorway, Chokhamela sings. His abhangas call Vitthal “Pandharicha raja,” yet they also ask why the king of Pandharpur lives behind human barriers.

i18n.hi: दरवाज़े के बिलकुल किनारे खड़े चोखामेला गाते हैं। उनकी अभंगें विठ्ठल को "पंढरीचा राजा" कहती हैं, और साथ ही पूछती हैं कि पंढरपुर का राजा इंसानी रुकावटों के पीछे क्यों छिपा है।

panels.shot: three-quarter shot beside gate pillar, Chokhamela singing earnestly, Soyarabai joining
panels.action: Leaning against the gateway pillar, Chokhamela sings with eyes shut, palms open in appeal, while Soyarabai stands beside him, her lips moving in quiet harmony.

dialogue.text: The abhangas do not only plead. They argue: “If you truly dwell in every heart, Vitthal, how can you be stained by my touch?” Song becomes theology spoken from the margin.

i18n.hi: ये अभंगें सिर्फ़ मिन्नत नहीं करतीं। सवाल भी करती हैं: "जब तू हर दिल में है, विठ्ठला, तो मेरे छूने से तू कैसे मैला हो जाएगा?" गीत हाशिये से बोली गई देह-धर्म की आवाज़ बन जाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside crowded temple hall, some devotees glancing uneasily toward doorway
panels.action: Inside the hall, upper-caste devotees stand before the image; a few glance sideways toward the door, faces uneasy, as the sound of Chokhamela’s voice drifts in like a steady current.

dialogue.text: Later hagiography will wrap this scene in miracles. Historians read more quietly: his verses were remembered, copied, debated—evidence that his presence disturbed the comfort of the hall.

i18n.hi: बाद की भक्त-चरित्र इस दृश्य को चमत्कारों में लपेट देती है। इतिहासकार धीमे पढ़ते हैं: उसके पद याद किए गए, नकल हुए, बहस में आए — निशान कि उसकी मौजूदगी ने सभा की सुविधा हिला दी थी।

panels.shot: close-up on Soyarabai, resolute, with temple gate behind her
panels.action: Soyarabai stands just outside the gate, spine straight, eyes bright, hands still from work as if claimed by a thought that will become a poem.

dialogue.text: Soyarabai answers in her own abhangas. She refuses the idea that Mahar birth is a spiritual stain, and complains of the endless labor pressed on her body and caste.

i18n.hi: सोयाराबाई अपनी अभंगों में जवाब देती हैं। वे महार जन्म को आध्यात्मिक दाग मानने से इनकार करती हैं, और अपने तन और जाति पर लादे गए अंतहीन काम पर शिकायत दर्ज करती हैं।

panels.shot: hut interior in Pandharpur settlement, both seated, composing, palm-leaf manuscripts nearby
panels.action: In a modest dwelling near Pandharpur, the couple sit facing each other, a palm-leaf manuscript between them, as if giving their words to a unseen circle of future listeners.

dialogue.text: The poems travel. Copied on palm-leaf, memorised by Warkaris, they carry the sound of a Mahar couple whose devotion cannot be separated from protest against injustice.

i18n.hi: ये कविता चल पड़ती है। ताड़-पत्रों पर नकल, वारी में याद होकर, वे उस महार दंपती की आवाज़ ढोती हैं जिसकी भक्ति अन्याय के विरोध से अलग नहीं हो सकती।

panels.shot: somber wide of riverbank near Mangalvedha, group of Mahars laboring, Chokhamela among them
panels.action: On the riverbank near Mangalvedha, Mahar workers haul stones and timber for a defensive work; Chokhamela moves among them, face set with quiet resolve.

dialogue.text: Mahipati’s Bhaktavijaya, written centuries later, places Chokhamela’s death while serving at a fort near Mangalvedha. The details are hagiographic, but they point to his life as village-service labor.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बाद लिखी महिपति की ‘भक्तविजय’ चोखामेला की मौत मंगलवेढा के क़िले की सेवा में दिखाती है। बातें भक्त-चरित्र की हैं, पर इशारा उसके गाँव-सेवा वाले जीवन पर है।

panels.shot: transition shot showing Soyarabai receiving news from a fellow worker, river flowing behind
panels.action: Soyarabai stands at the water’s edge as a fellow Mahar, tired and dusty, speaks to her with lowered gaze; the river moves steadily past, indifferent yet eternal.

dialogue.text: What is certain is less dramatic than legend: he dies as a Mahar worker. Hagiography will later imagine walls collapsing and singing bones. Historians keep to silence and survival.

i18n.hi: यक़ीन की बात कथाओं से ज़्यादा सीधी है: वे महार मज़दूर की तरह ही मरते हैं। बाद की हागियोग्राफ़ी दीवारों के गिरने, गाती हड्डियाँ गढ़ती है। इतिहासकार सिर्फ़ जीने और बचे रहने पर टिकते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Pandharpur temple gate with simple samadhi marker at threshold
panels.action: Years later, the Pandharpur temple threshold bears a small raised stone samadhi near the gate, pilgrims pausing as they enter and leave; the inner sanctum looms beyond.

dialogue.text: At Pandharpur today, a samadhi for Chokhamela stands by the gate. The memory fixes him forever at the threshold—neither fully inside nor outside the temple’s story.

i18n.hi: आज पंढरपुर में चोखामेला की समाधि फाटक के पास है। याद उन्हें हमेशा देहलीज़ पर बाँध देती है — मंदिर की कथा में न पूरा अंदर, न पूरा बाहर।

panels.shot: close-up of devotional singer at samadhi, with ghostly overlay of Chokhamela and Soyarabai
panels.action: A modern Warkari singer stands before the samadhi, eyes lifted, while faint, transparent images of Chokhamela and Soyarabai seem to watch from beside the stone.

dialogue.text: Across centuries, their abhangas keep being sung. Dalit thinkers in our time hear in them not harmless piety, but a sharp, early voice questioning caste inside a devotional movement.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक उनकी अभंगें गाई जाती हैं। हमारे समय के दलित चिंतक इनमें सीधी-सादी भक्ति नहीं, बल्कि भक्ति के भीतर जाति पर शुरुआती तेज़ सवाल सुनते हैं।

panels.shot: final wide shot of temple gate at dusk again, focus on threshold stone and pilgrims of many castes
panels.action: At dusk, the gate of Vitthal’s temple glows softly as pilgrims of many backgrounds pass the samadhi, some bowing; the stone threshold lies between their feet and the inner light.

dialogue.text: From Mehuna Raja’s fields to Pandharpur’s steps, Chokhamela and Soyarabai show how dignity can speak from the doorway itself—until, one day, the doorway must change to match the song.

i18n.hi: मेहूना राजा के खेतों से पंढरपुर की सीढ़ियों तक, चोखामेला और सोयाराबाई दिखाते हैं कि इज़्ज़त देहलीज़ से भी बोल सकती है — जब तक एक दिन देहलीज़ खुद गीत के मुताबिक़ बदलनी न पड़े।

subtitle_i18n.en: Songs at the doorstep of God
subtitle_i18n.hi: भगवान के द्वार पर गूँजते गीत
